evidence: ParseDocument parses with fences first and falls back to a fence-free parse only when a fence is still open at the end. The fallback pass cannot report an open fence, so it cannot loop or recurse.

fenceRun now rejects a backtick run whose trailing text contains a backtick, which matches CommonMark for opening fences. Tilde fences are unaffected, and a closing fence carries no info text, so the new check does not change closing behaviour.
The new test covers the three stray forms (```go, ```x``` text, ~~~) in Tasks and expects Decide to allow T1, which holds under the fallback.

One accepted trade-off, not a defect this commit introduces: a document with a real fence quoting a '## ' line plus a stray unclosed fence falls back to the pre-fence behaviour. That is exactly what the commit message and doc comment say.
